To get the best camera features, do you have to buy Apple's largest iPhone Pro? It depends on the generation. So far, most reports have indicated that there will be no difference in camera features between the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, but today a leaker has cast doubt on that claim.

Specifically, they say that two new features expected to be added to both Pro models will "probably" be exclusive to the Pro Max instead…

The iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max have the same camera specs, with three rear lenses all using 48-megapixel sensors. Apple says the telephoto lens offers up to 8x optical zoom, but this is actually achieved by cropping a 24-megapixel image, so it's more accurate to say it has 4x optical zoom with the option to output 8x images via cropping.

We have (basically) been expecting this year's Pro models to maintain camera feature parity, with both getting a variable aperture main lens and a wider aperture telephoto lens, the latter providing better low-light performance.

However, leaker Ice Universe says these two new telephoto features may be exclusive to the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

If true, this would mean that if you want the maximum telephoto reach and the best low-light performance, you'll have to buy the Pro Max. However, he used the word "probably," indicating he isn't fully confident in this claim, possibly because he's seen conflicting evidence in Apple's supply chain.

There are also reports that the variable aperture system on the main lens may be exclusive to the Pro Max, but reports on this are inconsistent.

If you usually prefer the smaller of the two Pro models, but could get better camera features with the Pro Max, would you choose to upgrade to the Pro Max? Let us know in the comments.
